claims.source_class: issuer licensing assertion and no-assurance qualification
claims.author_interpretation: Third-party IP is licensed in products/services; possible infringement notices and commercially reasonable license availability do not establish a particular dispute, term or remedy.
Customer purchases depend in part on third-party software availability; developer continuation and maintenance are not assured.
Developer choices may depend on relative platform benefits, market position, expected revenue/growth and costs; no developer utility or share is estimated.
Qualitative minority share may reduce developer incentives relative to competitors; no numerical share or causal elasticity follows.
Applications can fail to keep up with technology, operate incorrectly and reduce customer experience/demand; no incident or user cohort is identified.
App Store commissions, alternative purchasing, distribution, payment and developer-tool changes may affect sales or commission scope; the filing does not quantify a realised effect.

claims.source_class: contractual content-access assertion and no-assurance qualification
claims.author_interpretation: Third-party content arrangements can be short and need not renew on similar terms; providers may compete or raise access costs.
Own digital content can be costly and may fail to appeal; no content investment, cohort or demand probability is established.
Changing digital-rights requirements may require developing or licensing security solutions; cost, deadline and treatment are unknown.
Future success depends on team/key personnel amid intense talent competition and changing workforce conditions; no departure or probability is identified.

claims.source_class: management culture belief and conditional consequence
claims.author_interpretation: Management identifies culture as a success driver; inability to nurture it could affect recruitment, retention and results, without a measured channel.
Carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers distribute Apple and competitor products; direct and indirect routes remain distinct populations.
Carrier financing, instalment plans and subsidies may not continue or remain at the same amounts; no contract or subsidy amount is given.
Reseller programs incur costs and uncertain demand could reduce reseller ordering/marketing; no causal amount is computed.
Complex IT and supply-chain systems face listed failure/disruption causes; redundancy and recovery plans may be insufficient, without a particular incident.
Confidential-information use and security measures are described, but protection is not absolute; no breach or loss amount is established.
Sharing information with suppliers and third parties creates a separate exposure to their attacks and controls; no named incident is identified.

claims.source_class: historical attack assertion and conditional escalation
claims.author_interpretation: Malicious access attempts occur regularly and may increase in frequency/sophistication; this does not quantify a future incident.
Security measures may fail and third parties may induce unauthorised access, disrupting services/orders; affected records and costs are unknown.
Data-security insurance may address some risks but may be insufficient for all losses/types of claims; coverage, exclusions and recovery are unknown.
New strategies or acquisitions may distract management, create liabilities/regulatory barriers, reduce returns or impair/write off assets; no transaction is identified.
Retail exposure includes macro demand, construction/operation costs, partner relationships, inventory values and lease availability; no store history is selected.

ESG focus, company statements and external data can require investment and expose the company to changing standards, disagreement, liability or reputation effects; no legal duty or amount is inferred.
Data rules increasingly cover collection, use, retention, security and transfer and may conflict across jurisdictions; compliance costs and changes are not quantified.
Payment-card rules may create investigation expense, fees/fines or processing loss after compromise; no compromise or amount is established.
Margins and quarterly results vary with pricing, competition, demand, lifecycle, supply, costs, content, quality, mix, macro conditions and FX; no forecast relation is estimated.
Holiday seasonality and product/technology/logistics events can shift quarterly results; no allocation of a reported annual total follows.
Non-USD sales, costs and operating expenses create FX exposure; foreign supplier components can affect margins, without rates or exposures supplied.
Currency weakening can reduce USD sales/earnings and prompt price increases that may reduce demand; no pass-through or elasticity is known.
Forward/option hedges may not offset all adverse effects and cover only limited periods; instruments, notional and effectiveness are unknown.
Liquidity, credit, sovereign, rate and market factors may reduce investment value/liquidity; past lack of significant realised losses does not remove future loss possibility.
Tax rates, law, jurisdictional earnings mix and deferred-tax changes affect effective rates; OECD proposals and tax judgments do not establish Apple’s adopted rate.
Tax examinations may produce amounts above accruals; no audit outcome, rate or additional liability is identified.
Stock-price volatility can reflect expectations and market movements unrelated to operating performance; no stock-price path or repurchase loss is inferred.
